evidence.title: Hyperscaler capital spending accelerates
evidence.bounded_excerpt: Hyperscaler capital spending is accelerating for artificial intelligence data-centre construction.

evidence.title: Power queues constrain data-centre projects
evidence.bounded_excerpt: Power availability and grid connection queues constrain new data-centre projects while transformer equipment remains capacity constrained.

evidence.title: Transformer equipment backlogs remain firm
evidence.bounded_excerpt: Transformer equipment suppliers report firm backlogs and extended lead times while announced capacity additions are progressing.

evidence.title: Data-centre component demand broadens
evidence.bounded_excerpt: Compute, network and storage equipment demand is broadening alongside data-centre construction and electricity infrastructure requirements.

pattern.label: Data-centre power infrastructure constraint
pattern.definition: Accelerating artificial-intelligence infrastructure demand is meeting constrained power availability and transformer-equipment capacity.
pattern.what_changed: Company, industry and news evidence now independently connect hyperscaler capital spending with power and transformer constraints.

edges.mechanism: Artificial-intelligence demand raises hyperscaler capital-spending requirements.
Hyperscaler capital spending funds data-centre construction.
break_conditions: Capital spending shifts away from new data-centre capacity

edges.mechanism: New data-centre projects require grid connections and electricity infrastructure.
break_conditions: Data-centre construction becomes materially less power intensive

edges.mechanism: Grid expansion and connection work raises demand for transformer equipment.
break_conditions: Alternative grid technology substitutes for transformer equipment

edges.mechanism: Data-centre construction may raise demand for storage equipment alongside compute and network equipment.
missing_evidence: Storage equipment orders linked to new projects
break_conditions: Data-centre designs reduce storage equipment intensity

rationale.demand_impulse: Grid and connection work raises equipment demand.
rationale.revenue_exposure: Equipment suppliers derive revenue from transformer shipments.
rationale.volume_sensitivity: Revenue depends on shipment volume as well as pricing.
rationale.supply_responsiveness: Extended lead times indicate slow supply response.
rationale.scarcity: Backlogs and capacity constraints indicate scarce equipment availability.
rationale.pricing_power: Scarcity and firm backlogs can support supplier pricing power.
rationale.margin_sensitivity: Pricing and factory utilization can affect supplier margins.
rationale.capital_intensity: Expanding manufacturing capacity requires capital spending.
rationale.barriers_to_entry: Qualified grid equipment requires manufacturing capability and customer acceptance.
rationale.capacity_lead_time: Industry evidence reports extended lead times.
rationale.substitution_risk: The evidence identifies no near-term substitute.
rationale.public_market_investability: Public-company exposure may exist but is not mapped in the supplied evidence.
rationale.evidence_strength: Independent evidence supports demand and scarcity, while realized financial capture remains incomplete.

counterevidence.statement: Announced manufacturing capacity additions could ease transformer scarcity before current demand plans are completed.
counterevidence.rationale: The same evidence that reports backlogs also reports progressing capacity additions.

counterevidence.statement: Planned hyperscaler capital spending may not translate into completed projects if power access remains unavailable.
counterevidence.rationale: Capital plans and completed construction are different states.

data_requests.subject: Transformer equipment lead times
data_requests.reason: Lead-time history would test the persistence of the weakest scarcity assumption.

invalidation_conditions: Transformer lead times normalize while announced factory capacity becomes available
strengthening_observations: Backlogs remain firm while grid connection queues lengthen

what_changed.text: Independent sources now connect accelerating hyperscaler capital spending to data-centre power and transformer constraints.

why_it_matters.text: Power availability and grid equipment can become gating inputs even when compute demand and construction plans remain strong.

deliverable.transmission_text: Artificial-intelligence demand raises hyperscaler capital spending, which expands data-centre construction and demand for electricity infrastructure, transformer equipment and storage equipment.

potential_capture.text: Firm backlogs and slow supply response may support equipment pricing, while company-level margin evidence is still missing.

evidence_for.text: Grid connection queues and transformer capacity constrain new data-centre projects.
Transformer suppliers report firm backlogs and extended lead times.

evidence_against.text: Announced transformer manufacturing capacity additions are progressing.

weak_links_unknowns: Realized price and margin capture is not established
